problem:
The equation below describes all the points on the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ},$ where $P(-6,2,-1)$ and $Q(-8,0,-1).$

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 2 \\ a\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ b \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,t\in [0,c]
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Vector Equation of a Line Segment
examples.problem: Using $\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}$ notation, find a parametrization of the line segment $\overline{PQ},$ where $P(-4,1,2)$ and $Q(-2,5,-1).$
examples.worked_solution:
We need to find a direction vector that is parallel to the given line. We can use the vector $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{PQ} \\  & =\overset{\to }{OQ}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(-2\,i+5\,j-k)-(-4\,i+j+2\,k) \\  & =2\,i+4\,j-3\,k\end{aligned}
$$

So, the vector equation of the line is

$$
\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{p} + t \mathbf{v} 
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
\mathbf{r} = (-4 \, \mathbf{i} + \mathbf{j} + 2\,\mathbf{k}) + t (2 \, \mathbf{i} + 4 \, \mathbf{j} - 3 \, \mathbf{k})
$$

and the parametrization of the line segment $\overline{PQ}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =(-4\,i+j+2\,k)+t(2\,i+4\,j-3\,k) \\  & =(2t-4)\,i+(4t+1)\,j+(2-3t)\,k,\,t\in [0,1].\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Consider the straight line that passes through $P(3,1,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨2,1,3⟩.$ Find all the possible points $A$ on that line such that $AP=\sqrt{14}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the vector equation of the line, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =⟨3,1,-1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Since $A$ lies on the line, we know that there must be a real number $t$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{OA} & =⟨3,1,-1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

and 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PA} & =\overset{\to }{OA}-\overset{\to }{OP} \\  & =(⟨3,1,-1⟩+t⟨2,1,3⟩)-⟨3,1,-1⟩ \\  & =t\,⟨2,1,3⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,t,\,3t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the fact that $PA=\sqrt{14},$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}AP & =\sqrt{14} \\ |\overset{\to }{PA}| & =\sqrt{14} \\ |⟨2t,\,t,\,3t⟩| & =\sqrt{14} \\ \sqrt{(2t)^{2}+{t}^{2}+(3t)^{2}} & =\sqrt{14} \\ \sqrt{14{t}^{2}} & =\sqrt{14} \\ \pm t\sqrt{14} & =\sqrt{14} \\ t & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, putting the values $t=\pm 1$ into the equation for the line, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{1}}=⟨3,1,-1⟩+1⟨2,1,3⟩=⟨5,2,2⟩, \\  & \overset{\to }{O{A}_{2}}=⟨3,1,-1⟩-1⟨2,1,3⟩=⟨1,0,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the points are ${A}_{1}(5,2,2)$ and ${A}_{2}(1,0,-4).$
